decisions.title: Drop Node 0.8 support and require Node >=0.10
decisions.confidenceReason: The only stated message is "bump strip-ansi"; the support change is inferred from the engines field and the Travis matrix, and the package.json diff itself is cut off in the evidence.
decisions.context: Before af4983c the package declared engines node >=0.8.0 and ran CI on both Node 0.8 and 0.10. The commit is titled "bump strip-ansi", but it also changes the supported-runtime contract and several repository housekeeping files. The history does not say why Node 0.8 was dropped or whether the strip-ansi bump required it; the package.json patch is not visible in the evidence.
decisions.decision: af4983c raises the engines field to node >=0.10.0 and removes 0.8 from the .travis.yml matrix, leaving 0.10 as the only tested version. In the same commit, .gitattributes switches from `* text=auto` to `* text eol=lf`, .editorconfig gains a package.json rule for 2-space indentation, and the 1614-line logo.ai source file is deleted. The history gives no reason for any of these changes.
consequences: Node 0.8 is no longer declared as supported or tested in CI, so code may rely on Node 0.10 behaviour.
The support change sits under a commit titled "bump strip-ansi", so searching the log for a Node support change will not find it by subject.
Line endings are forced to LF for all files via .gitattributes, including on Windows checkouts; this is deliberate, not an oversight.
The Illustrator source for the logo (logo.ai) is no longer in the repository from this commit on, and the evidence does not show where it went.

decisions.title: Use supports-color instead of has-color for terminal color detection
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message is only "has-color => supports-color" and the diff shows a one-for-one dependency swap with no stated reasoning.
decisions.context: chalk exposed terminal color detection as `chalk.supportsColor`, backed by the `has-color` package at ^0.1.0. In 144421d that dependency was replaced by `supports-color` at ^0.2.0, and the readme link was updated from sindresorhus/has-color to sindresorhus/supports-color. The history does not say why the swap was made.
decisions.decision: Replace the `has-color` dependency with `supports-color` and assign its export to `chalk.supportsColor`. The change in 144421d is limited to the require in index.js, the dependency entry in package.json and the readme link; the public property name `chalk.supportsColor` is unchanged.
consequences: Color detection lives in the external `supports-color` package, so changes to detection behaviour belong there rather than in chalk's index.js.
`chalk.supportsColor` is a direct re-export of the `supports-color` module, so whatever that package exports is part of chalk's public API.
The readme documents that users can override detection with the `--color` and `--no-color` flags, and that text was kept unchanged across the swap.
`has-color` is no longer a dependency and should not be reintroduced alongside `supports-color`.

decisions.title: Add test coverage reporting with nyc and Coveralls
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff in b630e70 clearly show what was added, but no PR, issue or comment explains why these tools were chosen or why coverage was wanted.
decisions.context: Before b630e70 the project ran its tests with mocha on Travis CI and had no coverage measurement; the only scripts were `test` and `bench`. The history does not say what prompted adding coverage or why nyc and Coveralls were chosen.
decisions.decision: b630e70 adds nyc and coveralls as devDependencies and two npm scripts: `coverage` (runs `nyc npm test` then `nyc report` locally) and `coveralls` (runs the tests under nyc and pipes a text-lcov report to the coveralls CLI). Travis is configured to run `npm run coveralls` in `after_success`, and a Coveralls coverage badge is added to the readme. The `coverage` and `nyc_output` directories are added to .gitignore.
consequences: The `test` script stays plain `mocha`; coverage is only collected through `npm run coverage` or `npm run coveralls`.
Because `npm run coveralls` runs `nyc npm test` in `after_success`, the test suite is executed a second time on every successful Travis build, once for each Node version in the matrix.
Coverage upload depends on the external Coveralls service and on the Travis `after_success` hook, so it only happens for builds whose tests passed.
The badge URL added to the readme has an empty `branch=` parameter, so it does not pin a specific branch.

evidence.title: add coverage reporting using nyc and coveralls (Benjamin Coe)

decisions.title: Adopt XO as the linter and run it before the tests
decisions.confidenceReason: The diff clearly shows JSHint config being replaced by XO wired into the test script, but the commit message only says "add XO" with a link and gives no reasoning.
decisions.context: Before 409f95e the project carried a .jshintrc with a set of JSHint rules, and `npm test` ran only mocha. The code also already contained an inline ESLint directive in index.js for the deliberate `__proto__` assignment. The history does not say why XO was chosen; the commit message is just "add XO" and a link to the XO repository.
decisions.decision: Commit 409f95e adds xo as a devDependency, deletes .jshintrc, and changes the test script to `xo && mocha` so linting runs first and gates the tests. XO is configured in package.json under an `xo` key with the `node` and `mocha` environments. Existing files were adjusted to pass: benchmark.js gained `'use strict'` and a `/* globals set bench */` declaration, the index.js directive became `/* eslint-disable no-proto */`, and a stray blank line in test.js was removed.
alternatives: JSHint with a project-specific .jshintrc was the previous setup and was removed in 409f95e.
consequences: `npm test` now fails on lint errors before mocha runs, so style violations block the test suite.
Lint configuration lives in the `xo` key of package.json rather than in a standalone rc file; there is no .jshintrc to edit.
xo is pinned to `*`, so a new XO release can introduce new rule failures without any change in this repository.
The `/* eslint-disable no-proto */` in index.js and `/* globals set bench */` in benchmark.js are deliberate lint accommodations and should not be removed as noise.

decisions.title: Remove chalk.hasColor and chalk.stripColor along with the has-ansi and strip-ansi dependencies
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message only says what was removed and there is no PR, issue or comment giving the reasoning.
decisions.context: Chalk exposed two helpers on its export, `chalk.hasColor` and `chalk.stripColor`, which were direct re-exports of the `has-ansi` and `strip-ansi` packages. Both were documented in the readme and covered by tests. The history does not say why they were removed.
decisions.decision: Commit 04cae22 drops `has-ansi` and `strip-ansi` from package.json and removes the `hasColor` and `stripColor` exports from index.js, together with their readme sections and tests. Chalk's runtime dependencies are left as `ansi-styles`, `escape-string-regexp` and `supports-color`, and the export still exposes `styles` and `supportsColor`.
consequences: `chalk.hasColor` and `chalk.stripColor` no longer exist, so callers that used them will break; this is a removal of public API.
The removed helpers were thin re-exports, so the same behaviour is available by depending on `has-ansi` and `strip-ansi` directly.
The readme no longer documents the pattern of stripping colour from externally styled text when `supportsColor` is false, and chalk itself provides no helper for it.
Re-adding ANSI detection or stripping to chalk would mean reintroducing dependencies that were deliberately taken out in 04cae22.

decisions.title: Drop support for Node.js 0.10 and 0.12; require Node.js 4 or later
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff clearly show the support floor being raised, but no PR, issue or message body explains why it was done at this point.
decisions.context: Before 9b60021 the package declared `engines.node` as `>=0.10.0` and ran CI on Node.js 0.10, 0.12, 4 and 6. The commit subject says only "Drop support for Node.js 0.10 and 0.12"; the history does not say why the cut was made or why at this time.
decisions.decision: In 9b60021 the `engines` field was raised to `node >=4` and the 0.10 and 0.12 entries were removed from `.travis.yml`. The same commit updated dev dependencies: `require-uncached` was replaced by `import-fresh` in the tests, `nyc` moved from ^6.1.1 to ^10.3.2 and `resolve-from` from ^2.0.0 to ^3.0.0. It also added `*.js text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes`, removed the `package.json` override from `.editorconfig`, and changed `require('./')` to `require('.')` in the test and example files.
consequences: Node.js 4 is the minimum supported runtime; `package.json` declares `engines.node` as `>=4` and CI no longer exercises 0.10 or 0.12, so nothing verifies behaviour on those versions.

Tests that need a fresh copy of the module after changing `process.env.TERM` now use `importFresh('.')` rather than `requireUncached('./')`; new tests of environment-dependent behaviour should follow the same pattern.
`.gitattributes` forces LF line endings for `*.js` files, so checkouts on Windows will not convert them to CRLF.

`package.json` no longer has a two-space indentation override in `.editorconfig` and falls under the repository's general indent setting; the history does not say why this was bundled into the commit.

evidence.title: Drop support for Node.js 0.10 and 0.12 (Sindre Sorhus)

decisions.title: Convert the codebase to ES2015 syntax
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff make the change clear, but no commit body, PR, issue or comment states why it was made.
decisions.context: Before 249b9ac the library, its tests and its benchmark were written in ES5 style: `var`, `function` expressions, and `Object.keys(...).forEach` callbacks. CI ran on Node 6 and 4. The history does not say why the conversion was done at this point; the only stated intent is the subject line, "ES2015ify the codebase".
decisions.decision: 249b9ac rewrote index.js, test.js and benchmark.js to ES2015 syntax: `const`/`let`, arrow functions, `for...of` loops, shorthand methods and shorthand properties. The same commit added Node 8 to the Travis matrix alongside 6 and 4, removed `semver` from package.json, and reworked package.json, license and readme. A few small non-syntactic changes rode along in index.js: `styles` became `Object.create(null)`, the prototype function became an anonymous arrow function, and the Windows terminal check switched from a regex to `process.env.TERM.toLowerCase().startsWith('xterm')`.
consequences: The source now needs an ES2015-capable runtime with no transpile step visible in the evidence; Node 4 is the oldest version CI covers, so newer syntax should be checked against it.

Some ES5-style constructs were kept on purpose: `build` and the model getters still use `function` and `arguments`, the comment against slicing `arguments` for V8 optimisation remains, and `builder.__proto__ = proto` stays with an inline eslint disable because a function with a different prototype cannot be created otherwise.

The Windows terminal check now calls `.toLowerCase()` directly on `process.env.TERM`, whereas the earlier regex test did not call a method on that value; take care when touching it if `TERM` may be unset.
`semver` is no longer a dependency; the visible patch excerpt does not show what it was used for or why it was removed.

decisions.title: Replace mocha with ava and split the test suite into per-topic files
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff clearly show the runner swap and file split, but neither the message nor the visible patch states why ava was chosen over mocha.
decisions.context: Before 4c4eb1f (#182) all tests lived in a single 353-line test.js run by mocha via `xo && nyc mocha`. That file spoofed `supports-color` in the require cache at the top, and its Windows section mutated `process.env` and `process.platform` in before/after hooks and cleared `ansi-styles` from the require cache before each fresh import of chalk. The history does not say why the move to ava was made.
decisions.decision: 4c4eb1f swaps the mocha devDependency for ava, changes the test script to `xo && nyc ava`, and deletes test.js. The tests are redistributed into test/chalk.js, test/constructor.js, test/enabled.js, test/level.js, test/template-literal.js and test/windows.js, with a new test/_supports-color.js helper and the existing test/_fixture.js alongside them.
consequences: Tests now live under test/ split by topic, so new tests belong in the matching file rather than a root-level test.js.

Underscore-prefixed files in test/ (_supports-color.js, _fixture.js) are helpers rather than test files; the 13-line _supports-color.js was added in the same commit that removed the inline `supports-color` require-cache spoof from test.js, though its contents are not visible in the excerpt.

The Windows tests in the old suite depended on overriding `process.platform` and `process.env` and on deleting `ansi-styles` from the require cache because chalk modifies `ansiStyles.blue.open`; the evidence does not show how test/windows.js handles this, so check it before changing those tests.
ava is declared with the version range `*`, as mocha was, so the installed test runner version is not pinned by package.json.

decisions.title: Ship hand-written TypeScript definitions in the package and type-check them in the test script
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and an inline comment ("For TypeScript") state what was added and why the default export exists, but no PR discussion or message body explains the motivation for bundling types in the package.
decisions.context: Before f653b06 (#207) the package was plain JavaScript with no type information: package.json had no "types" field and the test script ran only xo and ava. The history does not say why the definitions were added to this repository rather than maintained elsewhere; the commit subject says only "Add TypeScript definitions".
decisions.decision: f653b06 adds a hand-written types/index.d.ts (credited in its header to Thomas Sauer), points the package.json "types" field at it and adds it to the published "files" list. It adds typescript as a devDependency and changes the test script to "xo && tsc --project types && nyc ava", so types/test.ts is compiled against the definitions (noEmit, noImplicitAny) on every test run. index.js also gains "module.exports.default = module.exports", commented "For TypeScript", so that the default import used in types/test.ts resolves at runtime.
consequences: The definitions are maintained by hand and list every style, colour and colour-model method explicitly, so any addition or rename in the public API in index.js must be mirrored in types/index.d.ts.
A TypeScript compile error in types/test.ts or types/index.d.ts now fails "npm test", because tsc runs between xo and ava.

The line "module.exports.default = module.exports" in index.js looks redundant but is deliberate (commented "For TypeScript"); removing it would break consumers using "import chalk from 'chalk'", which is how types/test.ts imports it.
Only types/index.d.ts is published; types/test.ts and types/tsconfig.json are not in the "files" list and exist solely for the repository's own type check.

decisions.title: Revert the lint fix that replaced \x escapes with \u escapes in the template tests
decisions.confidenceReason: Neither commit message gives a reason, so the record rests only on what the two diffs show.
decisions.context: 12d1276 ("Fix linting") added a file-level `/* eslint-disable unicorn/no-unsafe-regex */` to templates.js and rewrote three assertions in test/template-literal.js so that `\x78`, `\x6B` and `\x07` became `\u0078`, `\u006B` and `\u0007`. The rewritten tests include 'correctly parses unicode/hex escapes' and 'should not parse upper-case escapes'. TEMPLATE_REGEX in templates.js has a separate `x[a-f\d]{2}` branch for hex escapes alongside the `u[a-f\d]{4}` branch.
decisions.decision: 5282300 reverts 12d1276 in full: it removes the eslint-disable comment from templates.js and restores the `\x` escapes in the three test assertions. The history does not say why; the commit body only names the commit it reverts. The diff does show that the lint fix left the tests with no `\x` input in the touched lines, and made the second `keyword('blac\u006B')` assertion an exact duplicate of the line after it.
alternatives: Silencing unicorn/no-unsafe-regex for the whole of templates.js with a file-level eslint-disable comment was tried in 12d1276 and removed by 5282300.
Replacing `\x` hex escapes with `\u` unicode escapes in the template tests was tried in 12d1276 and removed by 5282300.
consequences: The `\x` escapes in test/template-literal.js are the only inputs in these assertions that exercise the `x[a-f\d]{2}` branch of TEMPLATE_REGEX, so do not normalise them to `\u` to satisfy a linter.
The paired `keyword('blac\x6B')` and `keyword('blac\u006B')` assertions look redundant but cover the hex and unicode forms separately.
templates.js carries no eslint-disable for unicorn/no-unsafe-regex after the revert, so whatever lint failure 12d1276 was addressing is not fixed by these commits.
The recorded dates put the revert (2018-02-14) a day before the commit it reverts (2018-02-15), so do not rely on date order when reading this part of the history.

decisions.title: Require Node.js 6 and adopt rest/spread syntax in place of arguments handling
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff clearly show the minimum Node.js version being raised and the code modernised, but no PR, issue or message body explains why Node.js 4 was dropped.
decisions.context: Before 0307f26 the package declared `engines.node` as `>=4` and Travis tested Node.js 4 alongside 6 and 8. The source was written around that floor, using `arguments`, `[].slice.call(arguments)` and `.apply(null, arguments)` for variadic functions in index.js and templates.js. The history does not say why Node.js 4 support was dropped at this point.
decisions.decision: 0307f26 raises `engines.node` to `>=6`, removes Node.js 4 from the Travis matrix, and rewrites the variadic code paths to use rest parameters, spread calls and destructuring (`chalk.template`, the colour model getters, `build`, `applyStyle`, `chalkTag`, and `buildStyle` in templates.js). The same commit bumps supports-color to ^5.5.0, updates dev dependencies (xo, nyc, execa, flow-bin, typescript), switches ava and xo from pinned versions to caret ranges, removes the `node`/`mocha` envs from the xo config, and renames the test import from `m` to `chalk`.
consequences: Node.js 4 is no longer supported or tested in CI; the code now relies on rest/spread and destructuring syntax, so anything added must only assume Node.js 6 or later.

`chalkTag(chalk, ...strings)` now collects everything after `chalk` into one array and treats `strings[0]` as the template strings array, so the tagged-template versus plain-call distinction depends on `Array.isArray(strings[0])`.

`build` creates `builder` as an arrow function that calls `applyStyle.call(builder, ...args)`, so `applyStyle` still depends on `this` being the builder even though the builder itself has no own `this`.
`.gitattributes` now forces LF line endings for all text files (`* text=auto eol=lf`) rather than only for `*.js`.

decisions.title: Extend the shared @sindresorhus/tsconfig preset instead of declaring compiler options locally
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message says only "Update dependencies and meta tweaks", so the decision is read from the shape of the diff and no reasoning is stated.
decisions.context: Before 4726b1b, tsconfig.json set its own `module: commonjs`, `target: es6` and `noImplicitAny: true`, and `typescript` ^2.5.3 was a direct devDependency. Flow warnings were made fatal by passing `--max-warnings=0` in the test script. The change arrived inside a general dependency-update commit, and the history does not say why it was made.
decisions.decision: In 4726b1b, tsconfig.json was changed to extend `@sindresorhus/tsconfig` (added as a devDependency at ^0.1.1), and the local `module`, `target` and `noImplicitAny` settings were deleted, leaving `noEmit` and `allowJs` as local options. The direct `typescript` devDependency was removed in the same commit. The Flow setup was also adjusted: `include_warnings=true` was added to .flowconfig and `--max-warnings=0` was dropped from the test script.
alternatives: Declaring `module`, `target` and `noImplicitAny` directly in tsconfig.json was the previous approach and was removed in 4726b1b.
consequences: Compiler settings such as module format, target and strictness now come from `@sindresorhus/tsconfig`, so upgrading that package can change type-checking behaviour without any edit to this repository's tsconfig.json.
Only overrides belong in the local tsconfig.json; the absence of `module`, `target` and `noImplicitAny` there is deliberate, not an omission.
`typescript` is no longer a direct devDependency and the evidence does not show what provides the compiler for `tsd-check`, so check this before relying on a particular TypeScript version.

Flow warnings are now included through .flowconfig (`include_warnings=true`) and the test script runs plain `flow` without `--max-warnings=0`; the evidence does not show whether warnings still fail the test run.

evidence.title: Update dependencies and meta tweaks (Sindre Sorhus)

decisions.title: Ship TypeScript definitions as a documented root index.d.ts tested with tsd-check
decisions.confidenceReason: PR #299 lists what was done as a checklist and links issue #293, but neither the commit nor the PR text explains the motivation, and the issue text is not in the evidence.

PR #299 was opened to fix #293, with a checklist covering doc comments, type renames and definition tests. The history does not say why these changes were wanted; the text of #293 is not part of the evidence.

Type tests move to index.test-d.ts and use expectType from the newly added tsd-check dependency. Per the PR checklist, ChalkOptions and ChalkConstructor are renamed to Options and Constructor, with aliases under the old names for backwards compatibility.

decisions.title: Replace `chalk.constructor()` with `new chalk.Instance()` for creating isolated Chalk instances
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff clearly show the change and a removed code comment shows the workaround the old approach needed, but no PR or issue text stating the motivation is included in the evidence.
decisions.context: Before de2f4cd (#322), a separate Chalk instance with its own `level`/`enabled` options was created through `chalk.constructor(options)`. The `Chalk` function had to cope with being called both with and without `new`, and a removed comment notes it checked `this.template` because "calling `chalk.constructor()` by itself will have a `this` of a previously constructed chalk object". The history does not say why the API was renamed beyond what the commit subject states.
decisions.decision: de2f4cd introduces `chalk.Instance`, a class (`ChalkClass`) whose constructor returns the result of a new `chalkFactory(options)` function, and makes `Chalk(options)` delegate to the same factory. `chalk.constructor` is replaced on every instance with a function that throws "`chalk.constructor()` is deprecated. Use `new chalk.Instance()` instead." The TypeScript definitions, Flow definitions, readme and tests were updated to the new name, with the `Constructor` interface renamed to `Instance`.
consequences: Although the commit calls it a deprecation, calling `chalk.constructor()` now throws an error rather than warning, so it is a breaking change for callers of the old API.

All instance creation goes through `chalkFactory`; `ChalkClass` is only a thin wrapper whose constructor returns the factory's result, so the returned object is the `chalk.template` function with a manually set prototype chain rather than a real `ChalkClass` instance.
The `this instanceof Chalk` / `this.template` branching in `Chalk` is gone, so new code should not rely on `Chalk` behaving differently depending on how it is invoked.

Type definitions expose `Instance` instead of `constructor` (`index.d.ts`, `index.js.flow`), and tests for instance creation live in the new `test/instance.js`, with `test/constructor.js` reduced in the same commit.

evidence.title: Deprecate `chalk.constructor()` in favor of `new chalk.Instance()` (#322) (Tom Sherman)

decisions.title: Require Node.js 8 as the minimum supported runtime
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff clearly show the Node.js floor moving from 6 to 8, but no PR, issue or message body explains why it was raised at this point.
decisions.context: Before 3ef170b the package declared `engines.node` as `>=6` and ran CI on Node.js 6, 8 and 10. The code carried at least one workaround for that floor: templates.js had a comment `TODO: Use Object.entries when targeting Node.js 8` above a loop over `Object.keys`. The history does not say why the floor was raised at this time.
decisions.decision: 3ef170b changes `engines.node` to `>=8`, removes Node.js 6 from the .travis.yml matrix, and starts using Node 8 features: `Object.entries` with destructuring in index.js and templates.js, and an async IIFE in examples/rainbow.js. The same commit bumps supports-color to ^6.1.0, updates dev dependencies (xo ^0.24.0, ava ^1.3.1, nyc, flow-bin, coveralls, @sindresorhus/tsconfig), and renames identifiers such as `args` to `arguments_` and `str` to `string`.
consequences: Node.js 6 is no longer declared as supported or tested in CI, so code in this package may use Node 8 features such as `Object.entries` and async/await.
The style-definition loop in index.js now iterates `Object.entries(ansiStyles)` and closes over the `style` object directly instead of re-reading `ansiStyles[key]` inside the getter.
The `Object.entries` TODO in templates.js is resolved and an `eslint-disable-line prefer-destructuring` comment there was removed, so neither workaround should be reintroduced.

The verbose names (`arguments_`, `string`, `characters`) arrived together with the xo ^0.24.0 bump; the history does not say whether the linter required them, but new code should follow the same naming to stay consistent.

decisions.title: Use a CommonJS-compatible export in the TypeScript definition, with types under a chalk namespace
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject states the intent and the diff shows the restructuring, but PR #344 only links to an external discussion (sindresorhus/meta issue 9) whose content is not in the evidence.
decisions.context: Before 98628d9, index.d.ts was written as an ES module: `Level`, `Options`, `Instance`, `ColorSupport` and `Chalk` were each top-level `export` declarations. The commit subject says the aim was a CommonJS-compatible export in the type definition. PR #344 gives no reasoning of its own and only points to a comment on sindresorhus/meta issue 9, so the history here does not say why in detail.
decisions.decision: 98628d9 rewrote index.d.ts so the public types live inside `declare namespace chalk` instead of being top-level ES exports. The level enum became a top-level `declare const enum LevelEnum`, re-exposed as `type Level = LevelEnum` inside the namespace. The same commit swapped the type-test dependency from tsd-check to tsd, updated index.test-d.ts to match, removed one line from index.js and added Node 12 to the Travis matrix.
alternatives: Top-level ES-module `export` declarations in index.d.ts were the previous shape and were removed by 98628d9.
consequences: New public types belong inside `declare namespace chalk`, not as top-level `export` declarations, or the CommonJS-compatible shape is lost.
`LevelEnum` sitting outside the namespace with a `Level` alias inside it is part of this restructuring; the excerpt does not show why it was split this way.
Type-definition tests in index.test-d.ts run with tsd, not tsd-check.

index.js lost one line in this commit and the patch excerpt is cut before showing it or the final export statement of index.d.ts, so check the full commit before changing how the module or its types are exported.

decisions.title: Replace per-call style arrays and close-code regexes with precomputed linked stylers and cached builders
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject of c08417e states performance as the goal and the diff shows the mechanism clearly, but no PR discussion or benchmark numbers are in the evidence and the patch is cut off before the new applyStyle body.
decisions.context: Before c08417e, each chained style getter built a new builder holding an array copy of all styles (`[...(this._styles || []), style]`), each style carried a `closeRe` regex built with escape-string-regexp, and `level`/`enabled` accessors were defined on every builder individually. The commit subject (#337) says the aim was to improve performance greatly; the evidence does not include measurements or further discussion.
decisions.decision: c08417e replaces the `_styles` array with a `_styler` object made by `createStyler(open, close, parent)`, which links to its parent and precomputes concatenated `openAll`/`closeAll` strings. Style getters now cache their builder on the instance via `Object.defineProperty(this, styleName, {value: builder})`, `level` and `enabled` move to the shared prototype and delegate to `this._generator`, and the builder coerces a single argument with `'' + arguments_[0]` as a commented hot path. The `closeRe` regexes and the escape-string-regexp dependency are removed, with `stringReplaceAll` and `stringEncaseCRLFWithFirstIndex` helpers added in lib/util.js.
alternatives: The previous design, removed in c08417e, kept a per-builder array of style objects and replaced close codes using precompiled `closeRe` regexes built with escape-string-regexp.
consequences: Builders carry `_generator`, `_styler` and `_isEmpty` rather than `_styles`; any code reading `_styles` no longer works.
After first access a style getter is replaced on that object by a plain value property holding the cached builder, so the getter does not run again for that chain.
The implicit string coercion in the builder (`'' + arguments_[0]`) and its eslint-disable are deliberate: the comment marks the single-argument case as the hot path.

String handling for close codes and newlines now depends on the in-repo helpers in lib/util.js instead of regexes, and benchmark.js was expanded to cover cached, newline and nested cases for checking future changes.

decisions.title: Move library code into a source/ directory and point package.json main at it
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message is only "Meta tweaks" and there is no PR, issue or comment, so the record is read from the shape of the diff alone.
decisions.context: Before 655653b the library's files were split between the repository root (index.js, templates.js) and lib/ (util.js), and package.json had no main field, so the package resolved to the root index.js by default. The repository also carried a tsconfig.json extending @sindresorhus/tsconfig with noEmit and allowJs. The history does not say why this layout was changed; the commit is labelled only "Meta tweaks".
decisions.decision: 655653b renames index.js, templates.js and lib/util.js into a single source/ directory, sets "main": "source" in package.json and replaces the individual file entries in "files" with the source directory. All tests now require '../source' instead of '..', and internal requires become './templates' and './util'. The same commit deletes tsconfig.json and drops the @sindresorhus/tsconfig devDependency, without stating a reason.
consequences: The package entry point is source/index.js via the main field, so new runtime modules must live under source/ to be published, since "files" lists only source and index.d.ts.
index.d.ts stays at the repository root rather than alongside the implementation, and is published separately through the "files" list.
Tests import '../source' directly rather than resolving through package.json, so moving the entry point again means updating every test file.
There is no tsconfig.json in the repository after this commit, so anything that type-checks the JS or the type definitions cannot rely on a project-level TypeScript config.

decisions.title: Require Node.js 10 as the minimum supported version
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and the engines/CI changes state the decision clearly, but no PR, issue or message body explains why Node.js 8 was dropped.
decisions.context: Before 61999a4 the package declared `engines.node` as `>=8` and ran CI on Node.js 8, 10 and 12. The history does not say why Node.js 8 support was dropped; the commit message is only "Require Node.js 10". The same commit also upgraded the dev tooling (xo ^0.25.3 to ^0.28.2, execa ^3.2.0 to ^4.0.0).
decisions.decision: 61999a4 raises `engines.node` in package.json to `>=10` and removes Node.js 8 from the .travis.yml matrix, leaving 10 and 12. Alongside this it adapts the code to the newer xo: variables are renamed (`ret` to `returnValue`, `errMsg` to `errMessage`, `str` to `string`), the `Instance` type in index.d.ts becomes a constructor type alias instead of an interface, and four lint rules are switched off in the xo config. It also rewrites the `level` option check in source/index.js so the validation only runs when `options.level` is truthy.
consequences: Node.js 8 is no longer declared as supported or tested in CI, so code here may rely on Node.js 10 features and should not be expected to run on 8.

The `// eslint-disable-next-line no-constructor-return` in `ChalkClass` in source/index.js is deliberate: the constructor returns the result of `chalkFactory(options)` and the lint rule is suppressed rather than the pattern changed.

The xo rules `@typescript-eslint/member-ordering`, `no-redeclare`, `unicorn/string-content` and `unicorn/better-regex` are turned off in package.json; the history does not say why, so check what they flag before re-enabling them.
The `level` validation now skips falsy values, so `0` and an omitted level pass without the integer check, while any truthy value outside the integers 0 to 3 still throws.

decisions.title: Require Node.js 12 and publish the package as ESM only
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and package.json signals state clearly what changed, but no PR, issue or message body in the evidence explains why.
decisions.context: Before fa16f4e the package was CommonJS: package.json had `main: source`, engines `node >=10`, source and tests used `'use strict'` with `require`, and the type definitions used a `declare namespace chalk` consumed via `import chalk = require('chalk')`. CI ran on Node 10, 12 and 14. The history does not say why the move to ESM was made at this point.
decisions.decision: fa16f4e converts the whole package to native ES modules and raises the minimum Node.js version to 12. package.json gains `type: module` and `exports: ./source/index.js`, drops `main`, and removes the import-fresh and resolve-from dependencies; Node 10 is dropped from the CI matrix. Source, tests, examples and benchmark switch to `import` with explicit `.js` paths, and index.d.ts is rewritten from a `chalk` namespace to top-level exported types (`Options`, `ChalkInstance`, `ColorSupport`, `ColorSupportLevel`, `Chalk`).
consequences: The package can no longer be loaded with `require('chalk')`; with `type: module` and no `main`, consumers must use `import`.
The `exports` field exposes only `./source/index.js`, so deep imports into other files of the package are not part of the public contract.

Type names changed shape: what was `chalk.Level`, `chalk.Options` and `chalk.Instance` in the namespace are now the top-level exports `ColorSupportLevel`, `Options` and `ChalkInstance`, so TypeScript consumers of the old names break.

import-fresh and resolve-from were removed along with test/_supports-color.js, so tests can no longer rely on re-requiring a fresh module copy or CommonJS resolution tricks; test/no-color-support.js was rewritten in the same commit.

evidence.title: Require Node.js 12 and move to ESM (Sindre Sorhus)

decisions.title: Ship type definitions from source/ via the `types` field, and measure coverage with c8 and Codecov
decisions.confidenceReason: Both diffs are clear, but the only stated reasoning is "Fixes #500" and "Fix code coverage"; the issue text and the nature of the coverage failure are not in the evidence.
decisions.context: Before 625a285 the type definitions (`index.d.ts`) and their tsd test (`index.test-d.ts`) sat at the repository root and were published via the `files` list, with no `types` field in package.json. Coverage ran through `nyc ava` with `coveralls` as a devDependency and a Coveralls badge in the readme. 625a285 says only that it fixes #500, and 7a68935 says only "Fix code coverage"; the history does not say what was broken in either case.
decisions.decision: 625a285 moved `index.d.ts` and `index.test-d.ts` into `source/`, added `"types": "./source/index.d.ts"`, and excluded the test file from the published package with a `!source/index.test-d.ts` entry in `files`. 7a68935 replaced `nyc` and `coveralls` with `c8`, so the test script is now `xo && c8 ava && tsd`, with c8 configured in package.json to emit `text` and `lcov` reports and to exclude `source/vendor`. The same commit added Node 16 to the CI matrix, added a `codecov/codecov-action@v2` upload step that runs only on Node 16, and switched the readme badge to Codecov.
alternatives: Coverage with `nyc` plus `coveralls` was the earlier setup and was removed in 7a68935 under the subject "Fix code coverage"; the history does not say what was wrong with it.
Type definitions at the repository root, published through `files` without a `types` field, were the earlier layout and were replaced in 625a285.
A direct `typescript` devDependency was added in 625a285 and removed in 7a68935, which added `@types/node` instead; the history does not say why.
consequences: The type definitions and their tsd test live in `source/` next to the implementation, and the `!source/index.test-d.ts` entry in `files` is what keeps the test file out of the published package.
The Codecov upload runs only on the Node 16 CI job and sets `fail_ci_if_error: true`, so a failed upload fails that job even when the tests pass.
`source/vendor` is deliberately excluded from coverage through the `c8` block in package.json, and the `lcov` reporter there is configured alongside the Codecov upload step.
`typescript` is not a direct devDependency after 7a68935; type checking of the definitions runs through `tsd` in `npm test`.

decisions.title: Remove tagged template literal support from the core chalk function
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject and diff make the removal and the pointer to chalk-template clear, but no commit body, PR text or comment in the evidence states the motivation.
decisions.context: Chalk could be called as a tagged template literal (chalk`{red text}`), parsing a brace-delimited style mini-language implemented in source/templates.js. Supporting this meant every builder call checked whether its first argument was a template strings array, and the factory returned a chalk.template function wrapped around the instance. The removed type documentation also noted that template literals were unsupported for nested calls (issue #341). The history does not say why the feature was removed.
decisions.decision: Commit c987c61 (#524) deletes source/templates.js, the chalkTag helper, the template-literal branch in createBuilder, the TemplateStringsArray call signature in index.d.ts, the readme section and the template-literal tests. The base chalk function is now a plain function that joins its arguments with spaces, and builders only stringify and style their arguments. The readme's Related section now points to the separate chalk-template package for tagged template literal support.
consequences: Calling chalk or a styled builder as a tagged template (chalk`...` or chalk.red`...`) no longer parses the {style text} syntax; the arguments are simply stringified and joined.

The ChalkFunction interface is gone from index.d.ts and ChalkInstance now carries only the (...text: unknown[]) => string call signature, so typings that relied on the template overload or on ChalkFunction will break.
Users who need the brace-delimited template syntax are directed by the readme to the chalk-template package rather than to anything in this repository.
createBuilder is now a single expression with the single-argument hot path, with no array check on the first argument; reintroducing template handling there would add a branch back onto that path.

evidence.title: Remove support for tagged template literals (#524) (Richie Bendall)

decisions.title: Vendor ansi-styles and supports-color into source/vendor and resolve them through package.json imports
decisions.confidenceReason: The diff shows clearly what changed, but the commit message is only "Bundle dependencies" and no PR, issue or comment states the motive.
decisions.context: Before 04fdbd6 the package declared two runtime dependencies in package.json, ansi-styles ^6.1.0 and supports-color ^9.1.0, and imported them by their bare package names from source/index.js and source/index.d.ts. The commit message says only "Bundle dependencies". The history does not say why the dependencies were bundled.
decisions.decision: 04fdbd6 removes the whole dependencies block from package.json and adds copies of both packages, with their type definitions, under source/vendor/ansi-styles and source/vendor/supports-color. A new package.json "imports" map exposes them as #ansi-styles and #supports-color, where #supports-color resolves to vendor/supports-color/index.js under the "node" condition and to vendor/supports-color/browser.js by default. source/index.js imports through those # specifiers, while source/index.d.ts uses relative paths into the vendor directory. The same commit renames source/util.js to source/utilities.js.
alternatives: Importing the types in source/index.d.ts from '#supports-color' is left commented out, with a TODO saying to switch to it once TypeScript supports that; relative vendor paths are used in the meantime.
consequences: The package no longer has a dependencies block, so changes to ansi-styles or supports-color do not arrive through a version range and must be made by editing the files in source/vendor.

Runtime code should import the vendored modules as #ansi-styles and #supports-color; the "imports" map is what selects the Node or browser build of supports-color, so a direct relative import would bypass that selection.
source/index.d.ts deliberately imports from './vendor/supports-color/index.js' rather than the # specifier, and the commented-out lines are a marked TODO, not dead code to tidy away.

The eslint-disable-line import/order comment on the './utilities.js' import in source/index.js was added in this commit alongside the # imports, and the helper file is now source/utilities.js, not source/util.js.

decisions.title: Keep a `main` field in package.json alongside `exports` for backwards compatibility
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message states the reason as backwards compatibility and references #536, but the issue text is not in the evidence, so what exactly broke is not shown.
decisions.context: The package is ESM (`"type": "module"`) and declared its entry point only through `"exports": "./source/index.js"`, with no `main` field. Commit 85f7e96 says a `main` field was needed for backwards compatibility and marks this as fixing #536. The evidence does not include the text of #536, so the history here does not say which tools or environments failed without `main`.
decisions.decision: Add `"main": "./source/index.js"` to package.json, pointing at the same file as `exports` (85f7e96). The `exports` field is kept unchanged, so both fields now declare the same entry point.
consequences: The `main` field looks redundant next to `exports` but is deliberate; removing it would reintroduce whatever was reported in #536.
`main` and `exports` must be kept pointing at the same file if the entry point is ever moved or renamed.
The package remains `"type": "module"`, so `main` resolves to an ESM file; this change does not add a CommonJS entry point.

decisions.title: Source style-name lists and types from the vendored ansi-styles and keep the old names as deprecated aliases
decisions.confidenceReason: The diff and its TODO/@deprecated comments clearly show what changed and that the old names are slated for removal, but the commit message (#567) gives no rationale.
decisions.context: Before 6e0df05, chalk defined its own style-name types in source/index.d.ts (`BasicColor`, `BrightColor`, `ForegroundColor`, `BackgroundColor`, `Color`, `Modifiers`) and built the runtime arrays `modifiers`, `foregroundColors`, `backgroundColors` and `colors` in source/index.js with `Object.keys(ansiStyles.modifier)` and similar calls. The history does not say why this was changed; the commit subject only reads "Export styles from `ansi-styles` (#567)".
decisions.decision: 6e0df05 makes the vendored ansi-styles (source/vendor/ansi-styles) the source of both the arrays and the types: chalk now re-exports `modifierNames`, `foregroundColorNames`, `backgroundColorNames`, `colorNames` and the types `ModifierName`, `ForegroundColorName`, `BackgroundColorName`, `ColorName` from it. The previous names are kept as aliases of the new ones, marked `@deprecated` in the type definitions and tagged with a TODO to remove them in the next major version. consequences: Adding or renaming a style means changing source/vendor/ansi-styles (both index.js and index.d.ts); chalk's own index files only re-export the lists and types.

The duplicate exports `modifiers`, `foregroundColors`, `backgroundColors`, `colors` and types `Modifiers`, `ForegroundColor`, `BackgroundColor`, `Color` are deliberate backwards-compatibility aliases, not leftovers, and should not be removed outside a major release.
The TODO comments are still present in the current code (source/index.d.ts:374, source/index.js:247), so the aliases remain pending removal in the next major version.
The type definitions import from the relative path './vendor/ansi-styles/index.js' rather than '#ansi-styles'; a comment in source/index.d.ts says to switch once TypeScript supports that.

decisions.title: Exclude vendored code from linting, test only on Node 14 and 26, and drop the Codecov upload
decisions.confidenceReason: The only message is the subject "Tweaks" and there is no PR, issue or comment text, so everything is read from the shape of a diff that is cut off at 7000 characters.
decisions.context: Commit 678e550 is a grab-bag titled "Tweaks" that touches CI, lint configuration, dev dependencies, types, examples and the readme in one go. Before it, CI ran on Node 18, 16 and 14 and uploaded coverage through codecov-action on the Node 16 job with fail_ci_if_error set. The package ships vendored copies of ansi-styles and supports-color under source/vendor, reached through the #ansi-styles and #supports-color import aliases. The history does not say why any of these changes were made.

The xo config ignores source/vendor and turns off no-warning-comments, and xo itself moves from ^0.57.0 to ^0.54.2. ansi-styles ^6.2.3 is added as a devDependency, while source/index.js still imports through #ansi-styles and source/index.d.ts still re-exports from ./vendor/ansi-styles/index.js. In the same commit the type declarations for modifiers, foregroundColors, backgroundColors and colors switch to the *Name types, and the readme's level 1 downsampling example changes from 31 (red) to 91 (bright red).

CI no longer uploads coverage to Codecov, so a coverage regression will not fail the build; c8 is still a devDependency.
Only Node 14 and 26 are exercised in CI, so breakage specific to the versions in between will not be caught there.

The xo range was lowered to ^0.54.2 rather than raised and the history does not say why, so check before bumping it again; likewise ansi-styles is a devDependency only, and the runtime code and types still use the vendored copy.

decisions.title: Require Node.js 22 and replace tsd type tests with a plain tsc check
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit subject states the Node.js 22 requirement and the diff shows each change clearly, but no message, PR or comment explains the reasons.
decisions.context: Before 8a94e0e the package declared support for Node.js `^12.17.0 || ^14.13 || >=16.0.0`, CI tested on Node 14 and 26, and type definitions were verified with tsd against `source/index.test-d.ts`. The package exposed its entry point through `main`, a string `exports` and a top-level `types` field. The history does not say why the Node.js floor was raised or why tsd was dropped.
decisions.decision: Commit 8a94e0e raises `engines.node` to `>=22` and changes the CI matrix to Node 22 and 26. It removes `main` and the top-level `types` field in favour of a conditional `exports` map with `types` and `default` entries. The tsd dev dependency and the 179-line `source/index.test-d.ts` are deleted, and the test script now runs `tsc --noEmit --types node source/index.d.ts` using a new `typescript` dev dependency. The same commit upgrades the dev toolchain (xo 4, ava 8, c8 12, execa 10 and others), converts the xo config to an array, and adjusts source and examples to the new lint rules.
alternatives: tsd with expectation-style type tests in `source/index.test-d.ts` was the previous approach and was removed in 8a94e0e; the history does not say why.
consequences: Node.js versions below 22 are no longer supported or tested, so code may use syntax that requires it, such as the regex `v` flag now used in the examples.

Type checking now only confirms that `source/index.d.ts` compiles; the removed `expectType`/`expectError`/`expectDeprecated` assertions about the public types have no replacement visible in the evidence.
The package entry point is resolved only through the `exports` map, since `main` and top-level `types` are gone; tooling that ignores `exports` will not find the entry or its types.

The `eslint-disable-next-line` comments in `source/index.js` for `unicorn/no-top-level-side-effects` and `unicorn/no-computed-property-existence-check` are deliberate: prototype setup and style getter installation must run at module load, and the `IS_EMPTY` read is a boolean value read.

decisions.title: Replace ava and matcha with Node's built-in test and bench runners
decisions.confidenceReason: The commit message is only "Meta tweaks" with no PR or issue text, so the change is clear from the diff but the motive is not stated beyond two code comments on specific details.
decisions.context: Tests ran under ava and benchmarks under matcha, both listed as devDependencies, with benchmark.js relying on matcha's global `suite` and `bench`. Commit 7211001 removed both packages and rewrote the tests and the benchmark. The history does not say why the switch was made; the commit message is just "Meta tweaks".
decisions.decision: In 7211001 the test script became `c8 node --test 'test/[!_]*.js'`, with test files importing `test` from `node:test` and asserting through `node:assert/strict` instead of ava's `t` object. The bench script became `node --experimental-bench --bench benchmark.js`, with `suite` and `bench` imported from `node:bench` and wrapped in a local `benchmark` helper that runs 10,000 operations per case. The same commit also bumped several devDependencies (xo 5, ansi-styles 7, setup-node v7) and made small edits in source/index.js.
alternatives: ava as the test runner and matcha as the benchmark runner were what was in place before and were removed in 7211001; the history does not record why.
consequences: New tests should use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` (for example `assert.equal`) rather than ava's `t.is` style, and the test glob `test/[!_]*.js` does not run files in test/ whose names start with an underscore.
benchmark.js sets `chalk.level = 3` deliberately: a code comment explains that the bench runner pipes stdout, so chalk would otherwise disable colors and only the plain passthrough would be measured.
The `benchmark` helper sums output lengths and throws on empty output, so every benchmark case must return the styled string it produces.
The bench script depends on Node's `--experimental-bench` flag, so it is tied to a Node version that provides that flag.

The `eslint-disable-next-line unicorn/prefer-ternary` in the builder in source/index.js is deliberate: its comment says a ternary would need nesting for the two- and three-argument cases, which `unicorn/no-nested-ternary` rejects.
